bib.title: HOTPOTQA: A Dataset for Diverse, Explainable Multi-hop Question Answering
bib.venue: Proceedings of the 2018 Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing (EMNLP), pages 2369-2380

question: How can a QA dataset be built that requires reasoning over multiple documents in natural language, gives sentence-level supporting facts, and is not limited to a knowledge-base schema?
hypothesis: Existing QA datasets fail to train systems for multi-hop reasoning and explanation; a crowdsourced dataset with supporting-fact supervision will be hard for current QA systems and the supporting facts will help them.
contributions: Questions that require finding and reasoning over multiple supporting documents
Diverse questions not constrained to any pre-existing knowledge base or schema
Sentence-level supporting facts for strong supervision and explainable predictions
A new type of factoid comparison questions

method.summary: Crowd workers on Mechanical Turk write multi-hop questions over pairs of Wikipedia first paragraphs chosen via the hyperlink graph (bridge entities) or from curated lists (comparison), and mark supporting sentences. A reimplemented Clark and Gardner (2017) reader with a supporting-fact classifier is trained as baseline in distractor and full wiki settings.
method.task: multi-hop extractive question answering with supporting fact prediction

datasets.name: HotpotQA train-easy
datasets.split: single-hop, part of combined training set
datasets.source: crowdsourced on Amazon Mechanical Turk via ParlAI over English Wikipedia dump of October 1, 2017
datasets.preprocessing: WikiExtractor for text and hyperlinks; Stanford CoreNLP 3.8.0 for word and sentence tokenization

datasets.name: HotpotQA train-medium
datasets.split: multi-hop questions the baseline answered correctly with high confidence in three-fold cross validation (60% of multi-hop examples)

datasets.name: HotpotQA test-distractor
datasets.split: hard multi-hop; 2 gold + 8 bigram tf-idf distractor paragraphs, shuffled

datasets.name: HotpotQA test-fullwiki
datasets.split: hard multi-hop; first paragraphs of all Wikipedia articles (5,000,000+ paragraphs)

models.name: Baseline reader (reimplementation of Clark and Gardner 2017)
models.architecture: character-level RNN and word embeddings, RNN encoders, bi-attention, self-attention, residual RNN, linear start/end token heads, 3-way yes/no/span classifier, plus binary supporting-fact classifier on concatenated first and last self-attention outputs of each sentence
models.context: 10 paragraphs (2 gold + 8 distractors) or top 10 retrieved

other.squad_gap: about 1 point worse in F1 than Clark and Gardner reported on SQuAD, without weight averaging

training.objective: answer span/yes-no loss jointly with binary cross entropy on per-sentence supporting-fact classification (multi-task, shared low-level representations)

other.full_wiki: model trained in the distractor setting is applied to the retrieved 10 paragraphs

inference.decoding: 3-way output decides yes / no / span; for span, search the most probable span
inference.retrieval: distractor: bigram tf-idf (Chen et al. 2017) retrieves 8 distractors with the question as query. Full wiki: inverted-index filtering to at most 5,000 candidate paragraphs (threshold N = 5000), then top 10 by bigram tf-idf.

metrics.name: Answer EM / F1
metrics.definition: exact match and token F1 of answer span, as in SQuAD

metrics.name: Supporting fact EM / F1
metrics.definition: EM and F1 on the set of predicted supporting sentences against the gold set

metrics.name: Joint EM / F1
metrics.definition: P(joint)=P(ans)P(sup), R(joint)=R(ans)R(sup), Joint F1 = 2PR/(P+R); Joint EM is 1 only if both are exact; averaged over examples

metrics.name: Retrieval MAP, Mean Rank, Hits@2, Hits@10
metrics.definition: rank of the two gold paragraphs in the full wiki candidate pool; missing gold paragraph ranked |Scand|+1 so values are upper bounds for MAP and Mean Rank
metrics.unit: % for MAP and Hits, rank for Mean Rank

baselines: ablations without supporting-fact supervision, self-attention, char model, train-easy, train-medium
eval.protocol: Human performance: 1,000 random samples from dev and test, at least three additional Turkers answer; original Turker treated as prediction, reference maximising F1 is chosen; upper bound uses each Turker against all others. No significance tests or seeds.

limits: Baseline hyperparameters (optimizer, learning rate, batch size, epochs, hardware, seeds) are not stated; only one baseline architecture is evaluated.
Authors concede their way of incorporating supporting-fact supervision is 'most likely suboptimal'.
Full wiki MAP and Mean Rank are upper bounds because missing gold paragraphs are ranked |Scand|+1.
Dev and test are filtered to be hard for the 2018 baseline; train-medium shares model-biased selection. About 6% of sampled questions are single-hop and 2% unanswerable.
Supporting-fact agreement among Turkers is lower than for answers, so that task is partly subjective.
Full wiki uses only first paragraphs of Wikipedia articles; results are for 2018 models and have long since been surpassed.
